newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels frustrate aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels frustrate aid workers.

text.p: Aid agencies in eastern Zaire said on Sunday efforts to help Rwandan refugees and others were frustrated by smouldering local conflicts and strict controls imposed by Zairean rebels who control the area.
Aid workers said the rebels had blocked aid convoys from travelling to areas outside Goma and imposed controls on the work of the agencies.
"Even when we have been officially given access to areas, we have found ourselves obstructed," said James Orbinski, head of the Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF, Doctors Without Borders).

The UN refugee agency UNHCR said it had located two large concentrations of Rwandan refugees and Zairean displaced persons at Lubutu, 200 km (120 miles) southeast of Kisangani, and at Shabunda, 150 km (94 miles) west of Bukavu.
"These people are trapped behind the Zairean government lines, areas where we have no access," one official said.

Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila denied in an interview last week his forces were hampering the aid effort. "They (aid agencies) are like tourists, looking around for their own curiosity," he said.

One Zairean aid agency estimated that at least 5,500 Rwandan refugees and Zairean displaced persons had died in the conflict in the Goma area alone since November 2. Many had been killed by Rwandan extremists trying to prevent the refugees from returning to Rwanda, it added.

Military success by Zairean rebels has failed to halt a series of local conflicts in rebel-held east Zaire. The conflicts, often pitting village against village, smoulder despite a two-month campaign of Zairean rebels against the army, aid workers said.
"What is really surprising is the level of ethnic mistrust from village to village. It really affects what we can do here," said a senior aid official.
At Kitchanga, a town of around 40,000 people about 60 km (37 miles) northwest of Goma, Hunde residents said they could not travel to the next town of Mweso for fear of being killed by Hutus.
"Rwandan Hutu militia came through and armed local Hutu population and showed them how to kill people," local Hunde dynastic chief Mwame Bashali told Reuters.
"If a Hutu goes to Kitchanga, he will be killed, and if a Hunde came here, he would be killed," a Mweso resident said.
The Mweso-Kitchanga conflict is representative of others in the region and has been complicated by the passage of tens of thousands of Rwandan Hutus through the area, aid workers said.
